reader.requirement: At --std 85 a format 1 REPLACE statement must replace every matched occurrence of each pseudo-text-1 (one or more text words, matched over text words across lines and separators) in the source program text within its scope by the corresponding pseudo-text-2 (zero or more text words, so an empty one deletes); the scope ends at the next REPLACE or at the end of the separately compiled program.

edition-consulted.switches: EditionInfo.ReplaceScopeEndsWithSeparatelyCompiledProgram (Year < 2002): a REPLACE's scope ends at the separately compiled program's end at 85, at the compilation group's from 2002
ConstructRegistry ReplaceAnywhere2002 (REPLACE must follow a separator period at 85) and ReplaceAlsoLast2002 (ALSO / LAST refused at 85)
EditionInfo.ReplacedTextIsLaidOutInFixedForm (Year < 2002): introduced lines take the replaced line's indicator and the continued-literal-on-debugging-line check applies
ConstructRegistry gate of the LEADING / TRAILING partial-word phrases (2002 constructs)
nothing: the text-word comparison is edition-independent

reader.edition-search: grep edition|Edition|ConstructRegistry|CobolVersion in CopyProcessor.cs and TextWord.cs; EditionInfo.cs properties ReplaceScopeEndsWithSeparatelyCompiledProgram / ReplacedTextIsLaidOutInFixedForm
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the replacement stops at END PROGRAM of the separately compiled program (rep4: REP4B keeps its MSG-X); at 2023 it runs on through the compilation group (rep4 at --std 2023 replaces MSG-X in REP4B's VALUE and is refused). The matching and substitution are the same code.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb1350_text_words_85 covers single-word and literal operands; it does not exercise multi-word pseudo-text-1 spanning lines, empty pseudo-text-2, several operand pairs, figurative constants/ALL literals, or the 85 scope end

probes.expected: §1985:XII.3.3 SR3 refusal of an empty pseudo-text-1; ALSO is no 1985 phrase

reader.notes: ApplyReplaceStatements finds each REPLACE and keeps an active operand set; ApplyReplacements substitutes every whole-word-sequence match with pseudo-text-2 (empty deletes), comparing text words with TextWord.MatchesForReplacing. Every probe printed the replaced program's expected output, and the 85 arms (scope end, fixed-form layout, ALSO/LAST and anywhere gates) behave per the 1985 text.

refuter.evidence: Probes under refute-1985-035/src at --std 85 via run_case.py, all MATCH: x1 (lowercase pseudo-text ==w-a== matches W-A, W-A-X untouched (whole text words), first pseudo-text-1 ==TAG A-B== wins over ==TAG== (GR6c), ==DISPLAY DUP== BY ==DISPLAY DUP DUP== not rescanned (GR6e), 'DISPLAY, W-Q' matched as 'DISPLAY W-Q' (GR6b separator comma), a comment line inside the matched source text ignored (GR7)); x2 (=='abc'== literal matches "abc" and NOT "ABC": III-3 NOTE 2 lowercase equivalence excludes nonnumeric literals; a match spanning a normal and a debugging line under WITH DEBUGGING MODE, and a word on a debugging line, replaced (GR8)); x3 (COPY text replaced by a later REPLACE (GR4); a continued nonnumeric literal in pseudo-text-1 matches a source literal continued at a different column (SR5)); x4 (literal containing == inside pseudo-text, a literal with doubled quote, semicolon separator, pseudo-text-1 ending in a separator period); x5 (a second REPLACE's own pseudo-text is not replaced by the first, and supersedes it). cite.py: OK §1985:XII.3.4 GR1, GR6b, GR6e, GR7, GR8.
